lead: Washington is cutting South Africa out of AGOA's duty-free trade benefits from January, a day before Wednesday's local elections. Special voting wraps up today after about 780,000 ballots on day one.

items.title: US removes South Africa from AGOA trade programme from January
items.summary: US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said SA and Rwanda will lose duty-free access, citing trade barriers and security concerns. Trade minister Parks Tau said SA has 60 days to respond and will help affected exporters find other markets.

items.title: About 780,000 special votes cast on day one; final day today
items.summary: The IEC apologised after 217 Cape Town stations opened late because ballot papers arrived late, and expects smoother running today. Special voting runs 8am to 5pm before Wednesday's main poll.

items.title: KZN approves nearly 349,000 special votes amid Newcastle registration claims
items.summary: KZN has the most approved home visits of any province. In Newcastle, a residents' forum alleges people were signed up for special votes without consent; three parties have gone to the IEC and the Electoral Court.

items.title: Two convicted over $580,000 Phala Phala farm theft
items.summary: The Modimolle court found Imanuwela David and Froliana Joseph guilty of conspiracy to commit housebreaking and theft at the president's farm, acquitting a third accused. The magistrate criticised the police investigation; sentencing is set for 13 November.

items.title: Poll puts MK well ahead in eThekwini as election nears
items.summary: One recent survey had MK at 48% in Durban, with the DA on about 25% and the ANC near 15%; nationally, polls show the ANC and DA roughly level at around a quarter of the vote.

items.title: Joburg Water asks residents to cut use by 15% as shortages spread
items.summary: Johannesburg's water utility warned that high demand is causing low pressure, intermittent supply and outages in parts of the city.

items.title: Learners evacuated safely as school taxi catches fire in Amaoti
items.summary: A minibus carrying Grade 1 to 4 pupils and a creche child caught fire north of Durban on Monday; the driver got all the children out.

items.title: Americans vote today in midterms with Democrats ahead in polls
items.summary: Recent surveys give Democrats a lead of seven to nine points on the generic ballot, while Trump's approval sits around 40% and most voters say they are unhappy with the economy.

items.title: Iran says it could reopen Hormuz within two days on its terms
items.summary: Tehran wants an end to fighting, unfrozen assets, lifted oil sanctions and an end to the US blockade of its ports. Qatar is mediating while Trump says some targets remain.

items.title: Yotova wins Bulgaria's presidential runoff
items.summary: Acting president Iliana Yotova took about 57% in exit polls against pro-Western Andrey Gyurov, who conceded. She favours diplomacy over further arms for Ukraine.

items.title: More than 200 arrested after Gen Z protests turn violent in Germany
items.summary: Mostly peaceful youth marches in over 30 cities over education funding, living costs and conscription ended in clashes in Hamburg, Frankfurt and Berlin.

items.title: US also strips Rwanda of AGOA and sanctions its defence ministry
items.summary: Washington accuses Rwanda of backing M23 rebels in eastern DR Congo, which Kigali denies.

items.title: DR Congo Ebola death toll revised to over 5,300
items.summary: Health researchers attributed the jump to a backdated data correction. The Bundibugyo strain driving the outbreak has no approved vaccine or treatment.

items.title: Rand firms and JSE gains as factory sentiment improves
items.summary: The rand traded near R16.64/$ on Monday while the Top 40 rose about 1%. Manufacturing sentiment edged up for a second month and new vehicle sales were up 10.4% year on year in October.

items.title: Citrus farmers warn of job losses after AGOA exit
items.summary: Growers fear losing ground to Peru and Chile. Agriculture envoy Wandile Sihlobo puts the extra tariff at about 3.4 percentage points, so the US market stays open. AGOA exports fell to about $1.7bn last year.

items.title: Fuel prices projected to drop on Wednesday
items.summary: Central Energy Fund data point to 95 petrol about 50c/l cheaper and diesel down roughly R1.58 to R1.68/l, helped by the temporary levy relief. The energy department still has to confirm the figures.

items.title: Oil falls on Hormuz deal hopes
items.summary: Brent fell about 2.8% to near $108.50 a barrel on Monday, and WTI dipped below $100, as traders priced in possible progress in US-Iran talks.

items.title: Settled Springbok side named for Italy test in Turin
items.summary: Siya Kolisi captains the team for Saturday's match. Salmaan Moerat returns from injury to partner Ruan Nortje at lock, while Eben Etzebeth and Cheslin Kolbe are out injured.

items.title: Pirates beat Chiefs 2-1 in Soweto derby to go top
items.summary: Yanela Mbuthuma and Tshepang Moremi scored for Pirates, either side of a Pule Mmodi equaliser, in front of a full FNB Stadium on Saturday.

items.title: Marquez wins in Malaysia to stretch MotoGP lead
items.summary: Marc Marquez took his seventh win of the season and now leads Jorge Martin, who missed the race with a wrist injury, by 44 points.

items.title: Apple sets China launch for Apple Intelligence
items.summary: Developer testing begins on 4 November, with a wider rollout in December alongside iOS 27.3. Alibaba's Qwen supports some features.

items.title: Judge lets NAACP pollution suit against xAI data centre proceed
items.summary: The case concerns gas turbines that allegedly run without permits and power xAI's Colossus facility. The ruling is procedural and makes no finding of liability.
